title: Chapter 35 — 'I Can Get It Cheaper Online': The Full Defence
intro: The defining objection of modern appliance retail — the complete-ticket line-up and price-match discipline.

sections.title: Acknowledge, Don't Argue
sections.content:
When a customer says 'I can find this cheaper online,' they are usually right about the number and wrong about the comparison. Your response should acknowledge, not argue.

'You are absolutely right that you can find lower prices online. That is a real number and I would never tell you it is not.'

Then reframe: 'The question is what that price includes. Let me show you what comes with our price that is not in theirs.'

sections.title: The Comparison Stack
sections.content:
Local delivery with a two-person team who brings it inside, not a freight truck that drops it at the curb. Professional installation by licensed technicians who verify gas lines, water supply, and electrical. Haul-away of the old unit — not your problem to figure out. A local person — you — to call if anything goes wrong, not a 1-800 number. Manufacturer warranty administered locally. No shipping damage risk — we inspect before delivery.

The math: 'If you buy online for $200 less, then pay $150 for delivery, $200 for install, and $75 for haul-away — you just spent $225 more and you have nobody local to call if the door panel arrives dented.'

sections.title: The Price Match Discipline
sections.content:
If they have a specific price from an authorized dealer, price-match it. The margin you lose on the unit you make back on attach and the lifetime customer relationship.

Never say the online price is wrong. Never trash the competitor. Never make the customer feel stupid for looking. They did their homework — respect it and then show them the full picture.

If you genuinely cannot match it: 'I understand. That is a strong price and I would never tell you to overpay. If you do buy online and run into any issues with delivery or installation, give me a call — I am happy to help you find a local installer.' This earns trust. Some of them come back anyway.
